detail.body:
## Problem and change

Persistent D128 FROST backward can reuse a completed dQ source-credit barrier phase without a successful wait. The store warp bootstraps four credits for each CLC work item, while the terminal dV/dK epilogue observes only slices 1 and 3. Slices 0 and 2 can therefore advance unobserved after the final dQ tile or a work item with no Q iterations. Ordinary numerical tests can pass despite this protocol violation.

Observe all four terminal dQ credit phases before publishing dV/dK. Apply the same repair to dense and THD accumulation loops; grouped-query kernels reuse those loops. Preserve the existing per-tile waits, TMA source-consumption waits and arithmetic.

Add eight regression cases covering MHA/GQA, causal/noncausal, FP16/BF16, both packed Stats layouts, persistent and zero-trip work, changed THD lengths/origins, poisoned storage and graph replay. Document the phase-observation requirement and synccheck detector in the SDPA agent guide. No capability row or public API changes.

## Performance hold

**Keep this PR unmerged pending performance investigation.** Reviewer measurements on two SM100 engineering devices found a repeatable dense-case cost for the added terminal waits: about +1.8% and +3.2% for FP16 causal MHA, B=3/H=6/Q=768/KV=1152/D=128. The ragged GQA control was approximately flat, and the separate host-enqueue checks did not establish repeatable added overhead. These are local complete-chain measurements with unlocked clocks, not production-B200 or context-parallel results.

The repair addresses a demonstrated synchronization violation. Passing correctness tests and review approval do not waive the performance hold; retain the required phase observations while investigating the cost. Broader host, device and full-CP non-regression qualification is still pending.

## Validation

At `dd9016cf347539c2cac7b0d4bd547fd2790dd79a`, based on develop `dde1f51c7a5b52d52cdaee4e9e512c2b579591b9`, with freshly built nanobind bindings on B200 (148 SM), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2 and CuTeDSL 4.8:

- The same regression on the unmodified base reproduces **2176 THD and 448 dense `Missing wait` errors** under synccheck. These intentional failing controls are recorded separately from numerical passes.
- **70/70 ordinary tests pass, zero skips:** the eight new cases plus the existing accumulation, THD and grouped-query suites. They use the existing FP64 reference and canary checks.
- **8/8 regressions pass under racecheck**, with zero errors and zero warnings.
- **8/8 regressions pass under synccheck**, with zero errors.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass. The original author validation covers correctness and synchronization; subsequent reviewer performance measurements are recorded below.

[Exact-source RED/GREEN synchronization evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v295_result.json).

**Draft: unfiltered memcheck qualification of the original pytest execution remains outstanding.** All eight numerical cases pass under memcheck, but the tool reports `CUDA API Warning: Selective device code recompilation in progress.` and exits with its configured error code. Eager module loading and compile-cache warmup do not resolve it. The retained stacks point to framework initialization or Torch reference/data preparation, including FP64 `masked_fill`; they do not establish a clean memcheck pass or assign a root cause. API error reporting remains enabled.

[Initial diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v290_rejected.json) · [Eager-loading diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v294_rejected.json) · [Warm-cache diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v297_rejected.json).

Run the regression from `test/python`, including the synchronization detector:

```bash
pytest -q -s -m L0 sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_d128_terminal_credits.py
CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck --error-exitcode 89 \
  python -m pytest -q -s -m L0 sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_bwd_d128_terminal_credits.py
```

## Exported native-chain memcheck diagnostic

The complete compiled FROST chains for all eight regression cases now pass **unfiltered memcheck with zero errors and no API warnings** in a standalone C++ process on B200. The target process loads neither Python nor Torch. It uses the exact 12 input fixtures and frozen FP64 references recorded by the unchanged public regression, covering dense/THD MHA/GQA, causal/noncausal, FP16/BF16, changed THD lengths/origins and both Stats layouts.

The independent plain control and memcheck process each complete **42 checked launches, including 24 CUDA Graph replays, and 126 gradient comparisons**. CPU comparison retains the original finite-value, cosine and elementwise tolerances, exact empty-row zeros, storage/workspace canaries and unchanged input buffers. Captured graphs verify the complete helper/main-kernel chains. No FE source, arithmetic or warning-reporting setting changes for this diagnostic.

This qualifies the exported kernel chains on the recorded fixtures. It does **not** qualify original Python preparation, all graph/binding APIs, or the separate TE integration under memcheck. The preceding exact-fixture Python replay still reports the runtime-recompilation warning in Torch workspace fill, despite passing all numerical checks; that result remains retained. No performance claim is attached to either sanitizer diagnostic, and the PR remains a draft.

[Native-chain qualification and frozen evidence](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_native_v308_result.json) · [Exact-fixture Python diagnostic](https://sc.talos.nvidia.com/view/home/scratch.yanxu_libs/cudnn_frontend/.te-cp-20261012/results/frost_credit_pr_v305_result.json).

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Exercise dQ source-credit reuse across live and zero-trip CLC owners.
+
+Numerics can pass despite an unobserved terminal barrier phase. From
+test/python, also run this file with CUDNN_TEST_NO_ISOLATION=1 under
+compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck --error-exitcode 89 python -m pytest -q -s.
+The pre-fix kernels report Missing wait on the store warp's next bootstrap.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import cudnn
+import d128_grouped_test_utils as grouped_utils
+import d128_thd_test_utils as thd_utils
+from frost_test_utils import requires_dsl
+from test_sdpa_bwd_d128_accum_sm100 import _require_accumulation
+from test_sdpa_bwd_d128_sm100 import _case, _check_case
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_dsl]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "grouped,causal,layout,dtype",
+    [
+        (False, True, "TH1", torch.bfloat16),
+        (False, False, "HN", torch.float16),
+        (True, True, "HN", torch.bfloat16),
+        (True, False, "TH1", torch.bfloat16),
+    ],
+)
+def test_thd_terminal_credits_replay(grouped, causal, layout, dtype, cudnn_handle):
+    _require_accumulation()
+    helper = grouped_utils if grouped else thd_utils
+    options = dict(dtype=dtype, causal=causal, stats_layout=layout, envelope=(1025, 1025), capacities=(4096, 4096), offset_dtype=torch.int64, units="elements")
+    options.update(dict(hq=6, hkv=2) if grouped else dict(heads=2))
+    case = helper.make_case((769, 0, 513, 1), (1025, 257, 0, 513), **options)
+    changed = helper.make_case((0, 641, 129, 1), (513, 769, 257, 1), seed=173, layout_shift=11, **options)
+    graph, refs = helper.make_graph(case)
+    pack = helper.variant_pack(case, refs)
+    workspace = helper.make_workspace(graph.get_workspace_size())
+    stream, ambient = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()
+    previous_stream = cudnn.get_stream(cudnn_handle)
+    capture = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        cudnn.set_stream(cudnn_handle, stream.cuda_stream)
+        for _ in range(2):
+            helper.poison(case, workspace)
+            stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+            with torch.cuda.stream(ambient):
+                graph.execute(pack, workspace.tensor, handle=cudnn_handle)
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+            helper.check_case(case, workspace)
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.graph(capture, stream=stream):
+            with torch.cuda.stream(ambient):
+                graph.execute(pack, workspace.tensor, handle=cudnn_handle)
+        helper.copy_case_storage(case, changed)
+        for _ in range(3):
+            helper.poison(case, workspace)
+            capture.replay()
+            helper.check_case(case, workspace)
+    finally:
+        capture.reset()
+        cudnn.set_stream(cudnn_handle, previous_stream)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grouped,causal", [(False, False), (False, True), (True, False), (True, True)])
+def test_dense_terminal_credits_persistent(grouped, causal):
+    _require_accumulation()
+    # 3 batches * 6 query heads * 9 KV tiles exceeds the B200 SM count.
+    # Causal owners beyond the six Q tiles have zero Q iterations.
+    if grouped:
+        case = grouped_utils.make_case((768,) * 3, (1152,) * 3, hq=6, hkv=2, thd=False, causal=causal, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        graph, refs = grouped_utils.make_graph(case)
+        pack = grouped_utils.variant_pack(case, refs)
+        guarded_workspace = grouped_utils.make_workspace(graph.get_workspace_size())
+        workspace = guarded_workspace.tensor
+
+        def poison():
+            grouped_utils.poison(case, guarded_workspace)
+
+        def check():
+            grouped_utils.check_case(case, guarded_workspace)
+
+    else:
+        dtype = torch.float16 if causal else torch.bfloat16
+        case = _case(dt=dtype, causal=causal, b=3, h=6, sq=768, sk=1152, accumulation=True)
+        graph, pack, workspace = case.graph, case.pack, case.workspace
+
+        def poison():
+            for role in ("dq", "dk", "dv"):
+                case.tensors[role].fill_(float("nan"))
+            workspace.fill_(0xFF)
+
+        def check():
+            _check_case(case)
+
+    for _ in range(2):
+        poison()
+        graph.execute(pack, workspace)
+        check()
+    capture = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.graph(capture):
+            graph.execute(pack, workspace)
+        for _ in range(3):
+            poison()
+            capture.replay()
+            check()
+    finally:
+        capture.reset()

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `dd9016cf3475` against base `3d3a2716f165`.

No approval-blocking issue found. This repairs a real synchronization-protocol violation: every dQ credit phase must be observed before the next owner arrives, even when ordinary numerical outputs happen to be correct. The new terminal waits establish that dependency through dV/dK publication for both live and zero-trip owners, and grouped routes reuse the repaired loops. Nonblocking: refresh the remaining draft wording in the now-ready PR description. Posting COMMENT because this is the author's account; an independent approval is still needed.

Validation: Reviewed the complete four-file diff and traced store/epilogue/MMA/scheduler phase progression, grouped delegation and zero-trip paths. Checked all 22 barrier declarations/33 active slots against issuing role counts (checklist A01/A02/A03/A07/A08, C04/C08/C09). The phase requirement is specified in [PTX ISA section 9.7.13.15.4](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.0.3/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#parallel-synchronization-and-communication-instructions-mbarrier-phase). Independently ran the exact-head regression on a native SM100 device with 148 SMs and CuTeDSL 4.8: 8 passed, zero skips. Coverage includes dense/THD, MHA/GQA, FP16/BF16, causal/noncausal, changed runtime lengths/origins, both packed Stats layouts, poisoned outputs/workspace, stream binding and repeated CUDA Graph replay against FP64 references. All eight exact-head cases also passed synccheck with zero errors. Reverting only the two kernel fixes reproduced 2,176 Missing wait errors in the persistent THD GQA control and 448 in the dense MHA control, each exiting with the configured sanitizer error code. The smaller THD MHA control has only 72 work items and does not force reuse on this 148-SM device; its old-code pass is not evidence against the bug. Bounded ABBA performance check of complete captured execution chains: dense causal MHA B=3/H=6/Q=768/KV=1152/D=128 FP16 increased from 44.35 to 45.14 microseconds (+1.8%); ragged causal GQA Hq/Hkv=6/2 BF16 changed from 63.77 to 63.94 microseconds (+0.3%). Separate CPU enqueue measurements showed no repeatable added overhead. Both revisions passed gradient checks before and after timing, including poisoned replay and THD canaries. These are engineering-device spot checks, not production B200 or end-to-end claims; the small dense cost is a reasonable correctness tradeoff. The current target base has unchanged consumed SDPA/FROST/binding/test source relative to this PR's merge-base. Exact-head Style is successful. The available PR SM100 CI selector currently uses DSL 4.7 and would skip this DSL-4.8-only regression, so I did not start a misleading all-skipped run; the native execution and synccheck results above supply the exercised coverage.

Limitations: Reused compatible compiled bindings for this Python-only change; the intended Python source was asserted at runtime. No independent racecheck or memcheck in this review, and no other GPU architecture was qualified. Performance is scoped to two warm workloads with unlocked clocks. The author's exported native-chain sanitizer qualification remains distinct from Python API/preparation qualification.
